title: Ex 3.7 #4(c) · 6-letter lists containing T, H, E in a row
prompt: Make lists of 6 letters from T, H, E, O, R, Y, with repetition allowed. How many of these lists contain the letters T, H, E consecutively and in that order, as YTHEOO does?
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4 or binom(10, 3).

mistakes.hint: The list THETHE contains the pattern in two places, so it is counted twice when you add up the four starting positions.
The block T, H, E doesn't have to start at the beginning: it can start in any of four places.

hints: The block THE can start at position 1, 2, 3 or 4. Count the lists for each starting position.
Can one list contain THE in two different places? If so, it has been counted more than once.
solution: Let $A_i$ be the set of lists with T, H, E starting at position $i$, for $i = 1, 2, 3, 4$. Each $|A_i| = 6^3 = 216$, since the other three positions are free.
Two blocks starting one or two places apart would force T to equal H or E, which is impossible. So the only overlap is $A_1 \cap A_4$, which contains just THETHE.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the inclusion-exclusion principle (Section 3.7).
